lessons: Tonight contradicted the guide: my BG deck with Spider Spawning, Vampire Interloper and Orchard Spirit still went 1-2, its flier answers thin (two Spidery Grasp, no Somberwald Spider); take one early.
Land count did not decide tonight: my 17-land BG deck lost R2 1-2 and R3 1-2, so evasion, not an 18th land, was the gap.
I ran exactly three evasive finishers, meeting the guide's minimum, yet lost; with ground bodies like Villagers and Lumberknot filling the deck, take a fourth flier or reach creature.
Fiend Hunter, my first-pick P1p1, never made the BR deck, so white was never a real option; commit to a first-pick colour pair early or take a flexible pick that fits the open colours.
Both of my losses came from fliers (two Stitched Drakes, Battleground Geist) that my BR pool couldn't block or remove beyond Harvest Pyre, so prioritize cheap flier answers in Innistrad.
Games 18 and 22 turns long against BG show my deck couldn't close, so favor evasive finishers like Crossway Vampire over grindy filler like Walking Corpse.
Against BR, my WG lost 0-2 despite two Slayer of the Wicked and Smite the Monstrous, so the guide's advice to block early and value two-drops over top-end is the thing to follow.
The guide says slow Moon Heron loses to BG, yet my two Moon Herons and Somberwald Spiders won 2-1 against BG, though my games were only 4-4 overall.
Guide says 17 lands with a low curve went 1-2, but my 17-land WG went 2-1 with 9 Forest and 8 Plains, so test 16 lands with this low curve before settling it.
Prioritise the Stitched Drake and Armored Skaab pairs: flyers and cheap blockers won the BR match 2-0 in 19 and 16 turns, while the 33- and 34-turn WG games showed grindy boards need a finisher.
Build the mana for your pips: this UB deck ran 11 Island and 6 Swamp despite Typhoid Rats, Walking Corpse, Diregraf Ghoul and Sensory Deprivation wanting black early; I'd go 9/8.
Cut-level fillers like Delver, Dissipate, Think Twice, Ghoulcaller's Bell and Lost in the Mist went unplayed; take a real two-drop or finisher over them in packs 2 and 3.
Ground filler sank my BR deck: two Manor Skeletons, Feral Ridgewolf and Gruesome Deformity lost long stalls, so the guide's Manor Skeleton skip was right; cap ground bodies at a few.
My BR had one flier (Bloodgift Demon) and went 0-2 in round 1 and round 3 stalls of 16 to 26 turns; take Falkenrath Noble or Morkrut Banshee evasion over a second Skeleton.
The guide's BR 55% did not hold: my Geistflame-heavy BR went 1-2 while seat 5's BR with Falkenrath Noble went 3-0, so BR needs fliers, not filler.
Prioritise cheap black removal (Dead Weight, Victim of Night, Tribute to Hunger) and early creatures; this BR deck went 6-0 in games with 15 creatures and Into the Maw of Hell on top.
Stop taking Burning Vengeance: I took two copies at picks 11 and 12 of pack 2 and cut both, so a second on-colour creature or removal spell was the better pick.
Four white picks (Rebuke, Moment of Heroism, Urgent Exorcism, Caravan Vigil) never made the deck, so once black-red was clear, take on-colour creatures over them.
Tonight contradicted the guide: my WU deck with 9 Plains and 8 Island went 0-3 against BR, BR and WR, so the 'WU 55%' figure and the 10-Plains anecdote did not carry over.
Four Delver of Secrets were weak early plays in my 0-3 deck, and games ran 16 to 21 turns, so Delver should not count as a removal-backed finisher or a cheap threat.
Against BR and WR aggro, prioritise on-colour two-drops and removal for fliers over the Delver copies and ground filler like Unruly Mob and Thraben Purebloods that filled my curve.
Don't assume a 17-creature red-white aggro curve closes out: my deck went 4-2 in games, but lost 0-2 to BR in 16 and 18 turn games, so draft more removal and finishers.
I left Charmbreaker Devils and Rage Thrower in the sideboard for curve, yet my round 3 wins came in 21 and 26 turns, so take the bigger late-game threat over another two-drop.
My two late Cobbled Wings picks never made the deck, while Riot Devils and Mausoleum Guard did; take playables in your colours over speculative pickups.
